claims: Pro-rata payouts on termination available after 5 years in NSW and after 7 years in QLD, WA and TAS; SA and NT pro-rata after 7 years; ACT after 5 years.
whys: The FAQ states these thresholds with no conditions. The site's constants (proRataUnconditionalFromYears: NSW 10, QLD 10, TAS 10, NT 10, ACT 7) say that below those years a payout is owed only on defined grounds, and a plain resignation does not qualify. The FAQ also types 8.67, 13 and 6.07 weeks as literals instead of reading LSL_JURISDICTIONS.
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's pro-rata question against the constants. proRataUnconditionalFromYears is NSW 10, QLD 10, TAS 10, NT 10 and ACT 7, so the FAQ's pro-rata thresholds leave out the grounds a payout needs below those years.

claims: Casual employees do not accrue annual leave, personal leave, or long service leave under the NES.
whys: State and territory LSL Acts cover casuals with continuous service. The site's own lib/constants/long-service-leave.ts sets casualsCovered: true (line 195 for NSW, with a casualsNote). As written, the FAQ tells casuals they get no LSL.
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's casual-LSL question. LSL_JURISDICTIONS sets casualsCovered: true in all 8 jurisdictions, yet the FAQ tells casuals they get no LSL.

claims: Award-free employees on individual contracts (common in professional services, banking, and technology) do not receive leave loading unless their contract specifies it.
whys: The parenthetical is a population claim with no source. Banking staff are often covered by the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award, which I believe has its own annual leave loading clause, so naming banking as typically award-free looks wrong. Suggest dropping or sourcing it. I removed only the hedge 'typically' because the rule (no NES leave loading without an award, agreement or contract term) is definitive.

claims: Annual leave payouts are taxed as ordinary income at your marginal tax rate.
whys: This leaves out the ATO rule that unused annual leave (and loading) paid on genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement is withheld at a flat 32%, as are pre-18 Aug 1993 amounts. The LSL calculator on the site already models the equivalent rule for LSL.
constants: ATO Schedule 7 unused leave rates (no constant for annual leave found; LSL equivalent is lslWithholding in lib/constants/long-service-leave.ts)

claims: Possibly. Annual leave payouts are taxed as lump-sum income at your marginal rate, which can over-withhold tax...
whys: This answer opens with a hedge ('Possibly'). It also contradicts the line 71 answer: one says payouts are taxed as ordinary income, the other calls them lump-sum income. Withholding on unused leave uses ATO Schedule 7, so the two answers should agree.

claims: This calculator uses {SITE_CONFIG.financialYear} rates and shows the tax on the lump sum.
whys: The calculator shows only 'Total Payout (Before Tax)' (line 154), and the methodology disclosure in leave-calculator-content.tsx line 319 says 'Tax on payout is not calculated here'. The hero claim is false. It is outside this unit.
